Double Fine’s 99-player launch, Picardo blames politics for Starfleet Academy, Xbox’s AI post and more | The Reef Daily 
https://t.co/tqS7NvCTX4

Tim Schafer at the 2018 GDC IGF Awards. Photo: Official GDC, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0 (cropped)

Double Fine’s new game, Thank You, Bus Driver, peaked at 99 players on Steam, and Kneon thinks the studio has bigger problems than its failed union drive. Also on the list: an Xbox manager who said everybody in games uses AI and then deleted his account, Robert Picardo’s newest reason Starfleet Academy got canceled and Taika Waititi’s Star Wars movie going on ice. Further down, the Halo remakes that reportedly never happened, Modern Warfare 4’s early reviews and the newest Clownfish TV podcast episodes.

New Clownfish TV episodes

How many people are playing Double Fine’s Thank You, Bus Driver?

Almost nobody. The game peaked at 99 players at once on Steam, according to the report Kneon reads, and by the end of the recording only 16 people were playing. For comparison, he points out that Concord had about 700. Less than a day earlier came word that Day of the Tentacle Remastered and Full Throttle Remastered are leaving Game Pass. Double Fine’s games had stayed on the service since the studio joined Xbox in 2019.

Then Kotaku piled on. Its report says a majority of eligible Double Fine employees filed for a union with the National Labor Relations Board earlier this year and withdrew the petition two weeks later. When 23 people were laid off soon after, Kotaku reports, all eight organizers who signed it were among them. Tim Schafer told Kotaku that “in general, I’m pro-union.”

Kneon’s read is simpler. Any indie developer could put a game on Steam and beat 21 players, he says, and a studio in that spot has to make games people will pay for first.

Did an Xbox manager really say everyone uses AI?

Yes, and then he deleted his X account. An Xbox business strategy manager posted that Microsoft uses AI “just as all companies do in 2026” and that developers who won’t use it shouldn’t be in the business. He also wrote, “I’m happy to take the hit if it means hundreds can stop pretending that they’re not using AI.” He deleted the account after the replies piled up, sources told PC Gamer.

Kneon agrees with him. Refusing AI now is like doing long division while everybody else uses a calculator, he says, and Microsoft spends too much on Copilot to keep it out of its games.

The episode also covers a report, built on anonymous sources, that more Xbox layoffs are planned for October, November and January. The same report puts Microsoft’s internal estimate for its next console, Project Helix, at $1,200 to $1,800 unless Microsoft subsidizes it. And some Xbox owners say Microsoft emailed them about trading their consoles in at Best Buy for up to $375.

Why does Robert Picardo say Starfleet Academy was canceled?

Politics, this time. Picardo said “the present political moment in our culture” made Star Trek’s core values “out of fashion temporarily.” Fandom Pulse counts that as his fourth explanation since Paramount+ announced on March 24 that the show would end after Season 2. The earlier ones blamed a lack of ads, Paramount’s new owners, Elon Musk and Stephen Miller.

Fandom Pulse also pulled the numbers. None of the first 10 episodes made Nielsen’s weekly streaming top 10, and by June the show had an 85% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes next to a 52% audience score.

Kneon has loved Star Trek: The Next Generation since he was about 10, and he says the show just wasn’t good. He calls it “a CW show in space.” Even Enterprise star Dominic Keating said on his own podcast, with Picardo sitting across from him, that it was “a bit CW in space.”

Is Taika Waititi’s Star Wars movie canceled?

On ice, in his words. Waititi told Inverse, while promoting Klara and the Sun, “we’re going to actually put it on ice and we’re working on a different thing altogether.” Kneon guesses Rian Johnson’s long-promised Star Wars trilogy is dead too.

The hosts also get into artist Frank Cho’s claim, made in a podcast interview at New York Comic Con, that he has been banned from Marvel for three years. “I pissed off Kathleen Kennedy and she demanded Marvel ban me,” Cho said. He says it started with joke Star Wars sketch covers he drew as convention commissions, and that Kennedy ended the whole Star Wars sketch cover program over them. Bleeding Cool, which reported the interview, couldn’t find new Marvel work from Cho after 2022.

The hosts expect a lot more stories like this now that Kennedy is gone from Lucasfilm. Somebody, they figure, will write the tell-all.

More news from D/REZZED

Halo Studios reportedly planned Halo 2 and Halo 3 remakes with full multiplayer. Halo YouTuber Rebs Gaming says the studio surveyed fans about Forge, Firefight and every classic playlist under the codename Project Manihi, and Windows Central says those plans are “pretty much dead in the water” after the Sept. 22 layoffs. No official comment has turned up from Microsoft. Read the story on D/REZZED.

Modern Warfare 4’s campaign reviews are strong, and early buyers on Steam rated it about 93% positive as of Monday. The full game, Switch 2 version included, arrives Friday, Oct. 23.

CNN and CBS News keep separate bosses under Skydance, but David Ellison says there are “absolutely operational efficiencies” to chase on the way to $6 billion in savings.

CNN also signed a multiyear AI deal with Google that pays it for its journalism. Neither side shared the price.

Ecto Cooler is pouring again from the Freestyle machines at the World of Coca-Cola in Atlanta, minus the neon green.

Linda Fiorentino played Agent L at the end of Men in Black, then left movies after a small 2009 comedy and never said why.

Nintendo’s Power Glove started as a $10,000 virtual reality glove that its designers rebuilt out of about $26 worth of materials.

And in Egypt, a man reported a carved stone outside his house, which led archaeologists to a colossal head of Ramses II.

Clownfish TV News Bites

From the Shorts archive: Doctor Who is getting a preschool cartoon, a 52-episode CBeebies series that could beat the main show back on the air. DC’s Supergirl finished behind Puss in Boots: The Last Wish on Nielsen’s streaming movie chart. Gears of War: E-Day got great reviews but is selling slower than Halo’s remake, at an estimated 230,000 copies in nine days. And Disney is blaming the live-action Moana flop on bad timing next to Moana 2.

Can we train language models to propose better ideas to improve LM—not just run them? 

Introducing 𝐋𝐌𝟐𝐋𝐌: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models. We train a 27B model with RL to propose improvements to language models. On held-out autoregressive and diffusion LM development tasks, it outperforms 𝐆𝐏𝐓-𝟔-𝐬𝐨𝐥 —at 33% lower data-generation cost. It also generalizes to a model family unseen during training.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐨𝐭𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐜𝐤: evaluating every proposal with a real training run makes RL prohibitively expensive.

𝐎𝐮𝐫 𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐚𝐜𝐡: a Research World Model (RWM) predicts experimental gains as a cheap reward signal. We periodically execute the current policy’s top proposals and add the measured outcomes to the RWM’s context, keeping its predictions calibrated as the policy evolves.

This is a step toward cheaper, more reliable feedback loops for recursive self-improvement (RSI).

I tested Seedance 2.5 to see how far I could push AI-generated content with a simple concept.

The workflow:
→ Generated a virtual character
→ Wrote a detailed prompt covering dialogue, actions, timing, and camera angles
→ Used Seedance 2.5 to turn the reference image and script into a 10-second video

The concept was simple: a girl and her boyfriend are carving pumpkins for Halloween. He finishes first and, when she reacts with surprise, tells her to try it on.

She puts his pumpkin over her head - only to realize she can't see anything because there's just one opening: for the mouth.
